newsitem.title: CHINA: Hong Kong people upbeat about future - survey.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong people upbeat about future - survey.

text.p: Most Hong Kong people are confident the territory will remain prosperous over the next year, according to a government survey released on Wednesday.
The upbeat vote of confidence comes just five weeks after the former British colony returned to Chinese rule.
In a survey by the Home Affairs Bureau that polled 1,527 people in July, 74 percent of respondents thought Hong Kong's situation would improve or stay the same in the next 12 months.
The figure was markedly higher than the 70 percent from a similar survey in May, the government said in a statement.
Some 77 percent of respondents were also satisfied with the present situation, little changed from 78 percent in May.
On the territory's future, 72 percent of people surveyed were confident that Hong Kong would continue to be prosperous and stable.
Fewer people, just eight percent, thought of Hong Kong's future as a problem, compared with 16 percent in May.
Half of those surveyed were satisfied with the performance of the post-colonial government, almost unchanged from the 49 percent in May, before the new government had taken office.
Housing was seen as topping the list of Hong Kong's most serious problems, the government said, followed by illegal immigrants and labour-related problems.
Hong Kong returned to China on July 1 after more than 150 years of British rule.
